t.7.1: The Blessed Lord said: With your mind attached to me, O Pārtha, practicing yoga and taking refuge in me, hear how you will know me completely and without doubt.
t.7.2: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge together with realized understanding, knowing which nothing further remains here to be known.
t.7.3: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection; and even among those who strive and have attained perfection, scarcely one knows me in truth.
t.7.4: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and also the sense of I: thus is this nature of mine divided eightfold.
t.7.5: This is my lower nature; but know, O mighty-armed one, my other, higher nature, distinct from this, which has become the living being and by which this world is sustained.
t.7.6: Understand that all beings have these two natures as their womb. I am the origin of the whole world, and likewise its dissolution.
t.7.7: There is nothing whatsoever higher than me, O Dhanaṃjaya. All this is strung on me, like clusters of gems on a thread.
t.7.8: I am the taste in the waters, O Kaunteya, I am the radiance in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in the ether, and the manliness in men.
t.7.9: I am the pure fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in the fire; I am the life in all beings, and I am the austerity in the ascetics.
t.7.10: Know me, O Pārtha, to be the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent, and I am the splendor of the splendid.
t.7.11: Of the strong, I am the strength that is free from desire and passion; in all beings I am the desire that is not contrary to dharma, O bull among the Bharatas.
t.7.12: And whatever states of being there are, whether sāttvika, rājasa, or tāmasa, know that they arise from Me alone; yet I am not in them, but they are in Me.
t.7.13: Deluded by these three states made of the guṇas, this whole world does not recognize Me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
t.7.14: For this divine māyā of mine, made of the guṇas, is hard to cross over. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond this māyā.
t.7.15: Evildoers, the deluded, the lowest of men, do not take refuge in me; their knowledge stolen away by māyā, they have resorted to a demonic nature.
t.7.16: Four kinds of virtuous people worship me, O Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of wisdom, O bull among the Bharatas.
t.7.18: All these are noble indeed, but the one who has knowledge is my very self; such is my view. For he, with a disciplined self, is established in me alone as the highest goal.
t.7.19: At the end of many births, the one possessed of knowledge takes refuge in me, realizing that Vāsudeva is all; such a great soul is very rare to find.
t.7.17: Of these, the man of knowledge, ever disciplined and devoted to the One alone, excels; for I am exceedingly dear to the man of knowledge, and he is dear to me.
t.7.20: Those whose knowledge has been carried away by this or that desire resort to other deities, adopting this or that observance, constrained by their own nature.
t.7.21: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, in each such person I make that very faith unwavering.
t.7.23: But the fruit of those of little understanding is finite. Worshippers of the gods go to the gods, while my devotees come to me.
t.7.22: Endowed with that faith, he strives to worship that form, and from it he obtains his desires, for those are in truth ordained by me alone.
t.7.24: The unintelligent think of Me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifestation, not knowing My supreme state, imperishable and unsurpassed.
t.7.25: Veiled by my yogamāyā, I am not manifest to all. This deluded world does not recognize me, the unborn and imperishable.
t.7.26: I know the beings that have passed away, those that are present, and those that are yet to come, O Arjuna, but no one knows Me.
t.7.27: O Bhārata, O scorcher of foes, through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, all beings fall into bewilderment at the time of creation.
t.7.28: But those people of virtuous deeds whose sin has come to an end, freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship me with firm resolve.
t.7.29: Those who, taking refuge in me, strive for liberation from old age and death know that Brahman, they know the whole of adhyātma, and karma in its entirety.
t.7.30: Those who know Me as the One who governs the elements and the gods, and as the Lord of sacrifice, they, with minds steadfastly united, know Me even at the time of departure from this life.
